samples.text: One awful conversation can leave you pretty certain you've finally figured somebody out. Then they come back later and actually deal with what you raised. They may still disagree with you, and you may still hate the boundary they're holding. I wouldn't know what to make of the first fight after that except that it was awful. What I'd watch is whether the same kind of ending starts showing up in completely different conversations. [Lindsay Gibson's work](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VlNpgFWOLPw) on emotional immaturity is helpful there. Different subject, same ending: somehow your experience is the part that never gets much room.

It doesn't mean you need to hide your upset, or apply for a permit to protest, but choose your battles and execute them wisely, so you don't end up regretting how you communicated later. As Lao Tsu might have said (if I could ever have read that whole boring Art of War book), a war with no casualties is the best possible war. When high IQ & EQ communication hits a writer's block, sometimes the best thing is to simply say, "I need some time to think about my response." And if the conflict really requires a response right now, then obviously just do your best rather than wait for the perfect timing.

Okay, write it. Write the unfair version too if that's what is there. The only rule is that it stays private for now. Later you can look at it and go, ugh, no, that's just mean. And then maybe two lines down there's the actual no you were trying to say. Keep that. If you owe an apology, put that in too. Sometimes the whole useful response turns out to be three boring lines. Sometimes, after all that typing, you don't really have anything to send.

I took exclusivity further than that. B. wanted to marry me, but I was still attracted to other women, and somehow I decided that meant I shouldn’t marry her yet. I told her, “It’s not fair of me to commit to you if I’m still attracted to other women, so before I do, let me see if I can fix that.”

Bear, sex can be what you do when you’re older and find a friend you love in a super special way that makes you want to raise children together. Don’t imagine you love each other just because you want each other. Don't feel pressure to promise commitment; it comes by itself naturally & honestly as your hearts sync. Learn about each other before getting too close, and make sure to keep friends and community around who know both of you.

My parents agreed with Somé that community matters and that we serve Spirit. They were also not romantic, though they were loving and poly. I actually wished they were in love with each other, I guess, although I couldn't have articulated that since I didn't even have that concept at the time. Also reminiscent of Somé, they also wore rose-colored glasses and taught me that everybody was basically good. So I learned something about love and community, but not how hard romance is without a community around it, or how much damage basically good people can do when their fears, trauma, and undeveloped parts take over.

And then there is the person who wrote the ugly version. Don't throw them out with the draft. Read it once more after you've decided what to send and ask what they were trying so hard to get heard. Maybe they needed protection. Maybe reassurance, or actual help. Maybe they were furious and still had a point. An angry first draft can be terrible communication without being a childish protest. Cleaning up what you send is one job; staying on that person's side is another.

This is a question I always ask myself. Why do people choose to use 5-MeO-DMT, instead of ayahuasca (or especially the Ultimate Psychedelic), considering that 5-MeO-DMT has no tradition of human use, much less therapeutic value, and is known to be very dangerous compared to ayahuasca?

So far, I have come up with a few answers (comment if you have others!):

Super entrenched ego, due to psychopathy, narcissism, and/or (c)PTSD, which blocks their ability to get powerful transcendental experiences from ayahuasca or meditation. Or, because they wish to avoid the moralizing guiding spirit (teacher) of ayahuasca.

They heard about it from someone and it seemed like it worked for that person, so they tried it and liked it, basically nothing to compare it to.

It’s vastly overhyped by some folks as being the God Molecule.

It’s harder to obtain than ayahuasca ingredients, which makes it seem more interesting.

It doesn’t have MAOi contraindications like ayahuasca, although it has its own set of dangerous interactions.

Some people’s neurochemistry is uniquely suited to 5-methoxy substituted tryptamines. These people find 5-MeO-DMT to be pleasurable, not frightening and toxic. The people who find it helpful for muting their emotional pain are also most at risk of abusing it.
